title: The delete class's new removal pattern misses a removal of kb content worded with another determiner or adjective, so a gate asking to remove kb content is no longer made blocking
goal: bl_authority's delete pattern matches a removal word (remove, removes, removed, removing, removal) followed by up to four other words and then kb, content or history, unless the words between hold flag, option or switch, so every probe of the repro is classed delete while the removed-flag design questions are not

run: import sys; sys.path.insert(0,"_tools"); import bl_authority as a; D=a.QUESTION_WORDS["delete"]; qs=["remove outdated content","remove the obsolete content","remove every kb page","remove this content","remove our content","remove unused entries from this kb","remove sources and kb pages","remove old, stale content"]; bad=[q for q in qs if not D.search(q)]; print(bad); sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)

import sys; sys.path.insert(0,"_tools"); import bl_authority as b; f=lambda q: b.class_reasons({"touches":[]},{"id":"g1","question":q,"options":["one","two"]})[0]; r=[f("Is the removed flag content-addressed?"),f("Is removal of the flag content-addressed?"),f("Are the old rows removed from kb history?"),f("Should we remove this content?")]; print(r); sys.exit(0 if r[0]!="delete" and r[1]!="delete" and r[2]=="delete" and r[3]=="delete" else 1)

notes: Found by the SP-uz3rhdlq review of BG-jw2cqoxa (reviewer gap, S3 as filed; fixed in the sprint as S2 because a delete-class guard failing open lets an agent go on without the operator). Choices settled in the goal: up to four words between, a flag/option/switch word in between stops the match; edit the pattern in place, one sentence each in backlog.md and tools.md.
